questions.question: The 3 umbrella workers each spawned ~10 sub-workers. What now?

options.label: Let it run, then triage the produced PRs (Recommended)
options.description: Don't kill anything. When sub-workers finish, they'll likely open PRs. Then I review which to merge vs hold. Useful memory-bank docs may be the highest-value output of this whole session.

options.label: Stop the cascade — kill remaining sub-workers
options.description: Kill the ~10 still-running children. Discard their incomplete work. Keep only what already committed + we'll PR those manually.

options.label: Let existing finish, but fire no more new dispatches
options.description: Let the 10 active workers finish naturally. Don't kick off any further rounds. Review whatever lands.

questions.question: While we wait, should I prepare the next round 4?

options.label: Yes — queue round 4 (verified-open, non-cascading)
options.description: Pick 6 more tickets that are unit-of-work (no umbrellas). Examples: dstrader-docker#6 (prod bug investigation), FF#34/#37 (password resets, deploy-track-aware), individual mb-* tickets that the cascade isn't already touching.

options.label: No more rounds until existing work clears
options.description: Wait until everything from rounds 1-3 (incl. cascade) is merged or stably reviewed before adding more. Lets you keep up with review load.

transcript_tail.text:
**I was wrong — the PR is actually correct.** Apologies.

Looking at the other mounts in the same compose file (`./dstrader-docker/dstrader:/root/dstrader/`, `./dstrader-docker/vnc:/root/.vnc`, etc.), this compose is run **from `$DSTRADER_ROOT`** (=`~/dev`), NOT from inside `dstrader-docker/`. `start_dstrader.sh:7` confirms it: `cd "$DSTRADER_ROOT"` then runs compose.

So `./dstrader-secrets/secrets/dstrader-docker` resolves to `~/dev/dstrader-secrets/secrets/dstrader-docker/` — which is exactly where the files were placed. **Path is correct, no fix needed.**

🎉 **PR #32 merged.** `.encr` files gone from `dstrader-docker` main, replaced by sibling-clone bind-mount. **dstrader-docker public-track gate cleared — the big unblock is done.**

Round 3 still: 6 workers active, none completed yet. Let me wait + check.

Monitor running. Will report when round 3 workers settle.

## Where we stand right now

| Round | Tickets | Merged | Held | Blocked → orchestrator pushed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | 10 | 3 audit PRs (FF#67, dstrader#34, docker#28) | — | (round 1 also had 5 collision-skips on already-done tickets) |
| **2** | 6 | 5 PRs (dstrader#35, docker#29/#30/#31, FF#68) + **PR #32 (.encr move)** | — | dstrader#14, FF#52, docker#27 |
| **3** | 6 (in flight) | TBD | TBD | TBD |

**Big public-track win this turn:** `dstrader-docker#27` merged → `.encr` files no longer in the daily-driver repo → public sync to `dstrader-docker-public` no longer blocked on the full SOPS prod migration. The deploy-track items (`#7`/`#8`/`#9`) can proceed on their own pace.

I'll report round 3 results when monitoring completes.

⚠️ **Worker over-spawn detected.** The 3 memory-bank scaffold umbrellas (#17, #23, #56) are firing off SUB-WORKERS for each child ticket (`mb-17-scaffold`, `mb-18-arch`, `mb-20-ops`, ...). Currently **11 active** instead of the 6 I dispatched.

The 3 umbrella scaffolds went wide — they're cascading into ~30 sub-tickets (one branch per memory-bank doc per family). ~15 already have a 1-commit each; ~15 still being worked. 4 sub-workers still alive plus the original 6.

Re-checking — the cascade is making progress, not just chaos. **`dstrader-docker#33` already merged** ("memory-bank scaffold — README.md + AGENTS.md root index #17") — the umbrella worker did its umbrella, then spawned children for the individual docs.

So what's happening:
- Umbrella worker `dstrader-docker#17` → ✅ scaffold merged as PR #33 → then spawned `mb-18-arch`, `mb-20-ops`, etc. (one sub-worker per child memory-bank ticket)
- Same shape on `dstrader#23` and `FamilyFund#56` — still running their umbrellas

Of 30 mb-* branches:
- ~15 have a single `docs: add memory-bank XXX.md` commit ready (no PR yet)
- ~15 empty (sub-worker still drafting or stalled)

No open PRs for any mb-* yet — sub-workers haven't reached the push/PR stage.
